en: So that's why you spoke to me.
Well, that's about the size of it.
And I do some hunting too. Trapping, though.
My traps are second to none.
My traps will feed you through the winter,
note: identical to M0#763 (slice 009) so the shared #764 'with no trouble at all.' works; one line

en: I see. What a shame.
Oh, it's you.
Usually I'm out here like this,
keeping watch over the hunting ground.
Don't come too near this area
and make trouble for me.
Is there something you need?
Yes. Even if I can't really hunt,
I was hoping you could show me
what kind of traps you make.
Well, if it's only a short explanation,
I don't mind doing that much.
Wonderful. Thank you.
My traps, you see,
are set to catch birds, but
now and then even a person gets caught.
That's dangerous, so I tell the villagers who go into the hunting ground
where I've set the traps
The poachers don't know about them,
so even if they slip past me and get in,
they walk into a trap and get nabbed.
Well, if you're that interested,
next time I go out to set traps,
I don't mind taking you along.
Really?
Yes, please. I'd love to.
Well, that much I can do.
Wait a little longer.
There's a right season for setting traps.
Then I'll take you along.
Osaida
I couldn't wait, so here I am.
It's urgent business...
I want you to take me right away.
Aaaaaagh
Well then, Osaida.
I'll be counting on you.
Yes.
What should I do?
Morning. You're up early.
Morning. Early again today.
Morning. You're always up early.
Well, hello there.
I'm on my way home now.
I'm heading home now. Care to come along?
note: msg 38043 continues with #887 (slice 011): 849 is 2 lines, so #887 must stay 1 line (e.g. 'Why don't you join me for dinner?')

en: If you like, let's have dinner together.
This is the house of me and my brother Vent.
I'm not much of a talker,
so if you want to chat, ask Vent.
It's nice to have a home where you can relax.
Obvious, I know, but I think so now and then.
I'm about to eat.
Hey. Glad you came.
Stay and eat with me.
Come by again any time.
I'm Jus, a carpenter.
I make furniture and the like.
Ah, pleased to meet you.
And you, friend? What's your name?
Me?
If you want something made,
wait a bit and come back later.
You wouldn't be thinking of trying
your hand at carpentry, would you?
If you'd help me out,
you'd be welcome, mind you.
The furniture around here,
most of it was made by me or my father,
or at least fixed up by one of us.
Plenty of what my grandfather made
is still around, too.
My brother Vent chops the wood for me.
Neither Vent nor I has a wife yet,
so we live together.
Come by our place, if you like.
